title: “They Want to Erase Us From the Digital Cloud”: Mixtec Engineer Asks Mexican Deputies to Use AI to Preserve Indigenous Languages
author: Iván Evair Saldaña and Enrique Méndez
content:
_This article by Iván Evair Saldaña and Enrique Méndez originally appeared in
the[September 14, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/14/politica/nos-quieren-
borrar-de-la-nube-digital-ingeniero-mixteco-pide-a-diputados-usar-ia-para-
preservar-lenguas-indigenas), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

![](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-15-at-10.09.14-a.m-1024x662.png)_Mexico
's Congress Channel_

**Mexico City**. From the tribune of the Chamber of Deputies, the citizen and
member of the Mixtec community Moisés Hilario López this Monday called on his
legislators to **modify the law to promote the use of technology and
artificial intelligence (AI)** in order to preserve Indigenous languages and
combat discrimination against their speakers. "They want to erase us from the
digital cloud," he pronounced in tu'un savi, a language also known as Mixtec,
while his words were translated simultaneously in writing into Spanish on the
large screen of the plenary hall.

Also a mathematics engineer from the National Polytechnic Institute (IPN) and
a specialist in science, technology, data analysis, and consulting, he took
part as part of the exercise "Indigenous Languages Take the Floor," held at
the start of each session.

Although during his speech the hall looked half-empty and most of the deputies
present were not paying attention to his intervention, Hilario López warned
that Mixtec children come to hide their language to avoid being mocked; that
Indigenous people who migrate to the cities are pressured to be ashamed of the
way they speak; and that this discrimination is also reproduced on social
media.

> If Artificial Intelligence can learn English, French, and German in a
> second, why don't they teach it Mixtec? Why isn't another Indigenous
> language taught? It's not a lack of technology, it's a lack of political
> will!

Hilario López proposed that the legislators take on **three state
commitments**. The first, he said, consists of allocating programs and budget
to create living digital archives of the native languages and to use the
voices of elders to train AI models. The second, requiring digital platforms
to detect and sanction hate against speakers of Indigenous languages; and the
third, financing artisans, creators, and teachers so that they can
commercialize and transmit, through technology, their knowledge and trades in
their own languages.

He also proposed creating a program called "Young Artisan Guardians of the
Language and Ancestral Knowledge," inspired by the federal program Youth
Building the Future, with the goal of generating income and preserving
traditional knowledge.

He closed his intervention with an invitation to visit his homeland, the
Mixteca Alta, to get to know its culture, taste its cuisine, and admire and
buy its art, from huipiles to sarapes, but "without haggling."

He emphasized that the ancestral knowledge of Indigenous peoples must be
preserved, beginning with their languages.

"They told us that our languages didn't fit in a book, and we survived. Today
they tell us they don't fit on the internet. They want to erase us from the
digital cloud, but they are wrong: because we are already of the cloud! **It
is no coincidence that our Mexica brothers called us Mixtecs, which in Nahuatl
means 'people of the clouds.' **We are children of the Ñuu Savi, people of the
rain. We come from the cloud, and the cloud cannot be erased or hidden," he
concluded.
